section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Body Esteem Scale (BES; Franzoi & Shields, 1984), a 35-item instrument used to measure feelings about body parts and functions on a 5-point scale. The scale has gender-specific subscales: for women, it measures sexual attractiveness, weight concern, and physical condition; for men, it measures physical attractiveness, upper body strength, and physical condition. The text reports internal consistency estimates (Cronbach's alphas) for each subscale, ranging from .80 to .89.
section_summary.evidence_source: Entire section describing the BES instrument and its psychometric properties.
